extracted.intended_audience: ICML 2026 authors, reviewers, area chairs, and senior area chairs
extracted.subtask_description: Official FAQ and procedural guidelines governing submissions, reviewing, rebuttals, COI, double-blind rules, reciprocal reviewing, LLM policy enforcement, reviewer/AC qualifications, and related workflows for ICML 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email sender addresses to expect
rubrics_metrics.description: Emails via OpenReview will come from noreply@openreview.net and icml2026-notifications@openreview.net.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure these addresses are not blocked by spam filters so you receive conference and review-related communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting prompt injection in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If you believe a reviewed paper contains a prompt injection by authors, first check whether the prompt was inserted by ICML organizers (used to detect LLM-policy violations) by viewing the footer text on page 2 of the reviewed paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prompt was inserted by organizers, disregard it and review as usual. If it was not inserted by organizers and appears to manipulate an LLM to obtain a favorable review (violating updated policy), report it by emailing program-chairs@icml.cc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling reviewer-cited prior non-archival versions anonymously
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer cites an earlier workshop/arXiv (non-archival) version that is actually the authors' own prior non-archival work, authors should not reveal identity in public rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave a confidential comment for the area chair stating that this is an earlier non-archival version by the same author(s). The area chair will ensure reviewers disregard the non-archival prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement form visibility rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The acknowledgement form button appears only when authors have submitted a rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no rebuttal was submitted you don't need to submit an acknowledgement form; if the button is missing despite a rebuttal, contact program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing reply button due to early reviewer edit
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors don't see a button to post a further response because a reviewer edited acknowledgement too soon, the reply button creation process may have been skipped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects only a small fraction of papers; organizers have manually fixed those instances. Contact program chairs if the issue persists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author AC Confidential Comments timing and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Author AC Confidential Comments are available during the author-reviewer discussion period for procedural/logistical comments and questions about reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These comments should not be used to submit extra rebuttals or late rebuttals after the March 30 deadline; such misuse will be ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author rebuttal: one response per official review
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can write one response to each official review (one response to each reviewer). Each response has a 5000-character limit and is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reviewers for the submission can see these responses; it's fine to direct reviewers to a response written for another reviewer when questions overlap. Deadline for author responses is March 30 AoE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer acknowledgement of author responses (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors posted a response, reviewers are required to acknowledge the response and agree to update the review in light of the response if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgement period starts March 31; the deadline for acknowledging authors' responses is April 3 AoE. Reviewers may also post additional comments/questions (5000-character limit) during this period; post early enough to allow authors to respond before April 7 AoE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' final responses to additional reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: For any additional comments/questions posted by reviewers after acknowledgement, authors can submit one final response to each reviewer via 'Reply Rebuttal Comment'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final responses have a 5000-character limit and the deadline is April 7 AoE. These final responses are optional and not expected if insufficient time is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling late reviews for rebuttal (special-case rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you received late reviews (after March 27) and couldn't rebut during the regular period, you may post a rebuttal via Author AC Confidential Comments by April 1 AoE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your AC must acknowledge receipt by April 3 AoE and will relay it to the relevant reviewer. You won't see the AC's official comment to reviewers or be able to reply directly; there will be no back-and-forth in these special cases—work closely with your AC to confirm sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICML watermark/prompt-injection detection policy in rebuttals
rubrics_metrics.description: ICML organizers inserted watermarking (a form of prompt injection) into PDFs to detect violations of the LLM policy; reviewers who flagged these should disregard them and proceed with reviewing as usual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer reviewers seeing such remarks to the FAQ link; authors/reviewers should not be penalized for the organizer-inserted detection prompt but should report non-organizer prompt injections to program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of reviews expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Over 99% of submissions had at least three reviews at the start of the author response period; a small number may lack three reviews and will receive emergency reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers will step in for papers missing reviews to ensure proper attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review scores vs review text importance
rubrics_metrics.description: What matters ultimately is the review text and not the final numeric score; ACs integrate all information from reviews and discussion into their final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not treat average score as a direct indication of final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective discussion strategy for rebuttals
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective responses focus on factual errors in reviews and on responding to specific questions posed by reviewers; responses should be reserved for cases when a response is called for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial response by March 30 should contain all arguments you wish to convey regarding the reviews; additional discussion should not raise new arguments beyond those points.

rubrics_metrics.name: No submission updates during discussion period
rubrics_metrics.description: The original submission (PDF and supplemental material) cannot be revised in OpenReview during the discussion period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must use their 5000-character author responses to provide corrections or missing details rather than uploading revised manuscripts or sections; reviewers and ACs are instructed to disregard any PDFs that contain revised manuscripts or revised sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and use of links in rebuttals
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses to reviewers should not contain or link to any identifying information that may violate double-blind reviewing policy; while links are allowed, reviewers are not required to follow them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links should be used primarily for figures (including tables) and their captions and to provide missing details (or minor corrections) of the submitted work rather than to present new work. All links must be anonymous in both URL and destination to preserve double-blind review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting of reviews and responses
rubrics_metrics.description: For accepted papers (and for rejected papers that opt-in), reviews and responses posted to reviewers will be made public at the end of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When posting messages during discussion, avoid writing anything you would not want made public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism in discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the review and discussion process, participants should be respectful and professional and abide by the ICML code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link provided to the Code of Conduct; unprofessional behaviour is discouraged and subject to community standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM policy assignment and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy assignment (Policy A vs B) was based on information provided in reviewer registration; it is each reviewer's responsibility to verify and comply with their assigned Actual Policy before and during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy assignment is visible in the Reviewers Console and in reminders on manuscript PDFs; reviewers must follow their assigned policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection process for Policy A LLM violations
rubrics_metrics.description: A rigorous multi-stage watermarking process was used: each submitted PDF was modified by inserting machine-readable instructions; if an LLM produced the two specific phrases in the review (chosen randomly), the review was flagged and manually checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organizers report a very small family-wise error rate (0.0001) for falsely flagging reviews under Policy A. If flagged, reversal is unlikely because the method includes manual checks to rule out mere noticing of the prompt injection.

rubrics_metrics.name: No exceptions to Policy A enforcement for partial LLM use
rubrics_metrics.description: Under ICML 2026's Policy A, the use of LLMs at any stage is strictly prohibited (including feeding submissions, whole or part, to an LLM), and no exceptions are granted based on degree of LLM involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even light use (e.g., for editing or understanding) that involved feeding the submission to an LLM can trigger policy enforcement; uniform enforcement preserves fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship/co-author consequences for LLM policy breaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of the LLM policy by a reviewer can be grounds for desk rejection of papers co-authored by that reviewer; co-authors of a violating reviewer may also be affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All authors agree to peer-review ethics which explicitly state these consequences; questions or appeals should be directed to program chairs, but uniform enforcement is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal reviewing: mandatory-review conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: You MUST review if any of the specific conditions apply: (a) you are listed on any full submission at the full submission deadline as a reciprocal reviewer AND you selected 'This submission is NOT exempt from the Reciprocal Reviewing requirement' AND you have not submitted a Reciprocal Reviewing Correction form with a different reciprocal reviewer; (b) you are listed on any full submission at the full submission deadline as a reciprocal reviewer submitted via the Reciprocal Reviewing Correction form; (c) you will be an author on at least 4 full submissions at the full submission deadline and you have not filed the Per-author Reciprocal Reviewing Exemption form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you find you don't need to review but have filled registration, contact program-chairs@icml.cc. Reminder emails may continue until Feb 3 while removals are processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal reviewing: exemptions and not-required-to-review conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: You DON'T need to review if any of the following apply: (a) all papers that list you as reciprocal reviewer have been or will be withdrawn or desk rejected by the full submission deadline AND you will not be an author on 4 or more full submissions; (b) you will have less than 4 submissions and the papers on which you were listed submitted the Reciprocal Reviewing Correction form with other reviewers or with exemptions; (c) you will have 4 or more full submissions but have filled out the Per-author Reciprocal Reviewing Exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are not required to review and do not plan to register, please do not bid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer registration deadline and requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you would like to be a reviewer or are required to be a reviewer according to reciprocal-reviewing criteria, you MUST fill out the Reviewer Registration form by Thursday Jan 29th AoE (24 hours after full submission deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access the form via the 'Registration' task in the ICML Reviewers group on OpenReview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal reviewer correction and qualification handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If your reciprocal reviewer nomination is unqualified, ensure the reciprocal reviewer fills out the Reviewer Registration form so organizers can filter out unqualified reviewers; good-faith nominations that don't meet criteria won't be penalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reciprocal reviewer is an AC, good-faith nominations won't be penalized and the AC will remain in the AC pool and won't be required to serve as a reviewer. Corrections submitted will override original values as long as 'correction' fields are visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding guidance and affinity scores
rubrics_metrics.description: If the bidding list contains many out-of-domain papers, it may be because you were added after affinities were computed; affinities will be recomputed after full paper deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update your expertise by the full paper deadline to improve bidding sets and include only relevant papers. Program chairs may broaden reviewer criteria and will notify by Feb 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area Chair (AC) qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs must have seniority at least at the level of a junior faculty member (e.g., assistant professor) or an industry equivalent, substantial prior reviewing experience, and expertise and/or broad knowledge in multiple major sub-areas of machine learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seniority and reviewing experience ensure ACs can oversee reviewers and make acceptance/rejection recommendations; expertise ensures they can judge contributions relative to prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: How ACs communicate with authors
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs can communicate with authors via the 'Author AC Confidential Comments' button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this channel for procedural/logistical matters; not for extra rebuttals outside the allowed windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must have research experience equivalent to a second-year graduate student in machine learning or a related field and must have been a primary author on at least two peer-reviewed conference or journal papers published in a related venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-time reviewers are strongly encouraged to identify a mentor (advisor or manager) with prior reviewing experience to oversee and assist. 'Primary author' is left to reviewers' discretion across sub-areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing load expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Target reviewing load is around 5-6 submissions per reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduced load reviewing is not being allowed this year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent ICML submissions: which to cite
rubrics_metrics.description: You should cite and discuss all of your concurrent submissions that a reasonable reader/reviewer might expect to see in a related work section (e.g., if one submission builds on another it must be cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether a reader seeing titles/abstracts side-by-side would wonder how the papers differ; if yes, cross-cite and discuss. Anonymized PDFs of all cited concurrent submissions must be provided in the supplementary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent submission citation format and supplementary handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymized PDFs of cited concurrent submissions must be in the supplement; suggested citation format includes an @misc entry with 'Anonymous Authors' and a note with the filename in supplement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default plan is to publish originally submitted supplementary material for accepted papers, but authors will be able to request exceptions (e.g., if referenced concurrent work is rejected and not directly built upon).

rubrics_metrics.name: Author accounts and deadlines for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must have (active or inactive) OpenReview accounts by the abstract deadline; the submitting author's account must be active by the abstract deadline and other authors' accounts by the submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create accounts well before deadlines; OpenReview processes account validations FIFO and cannot be expedited by program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: No extensions for missed deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines (abstract/full paper) are strict with no exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan submissions accordingly; late exceptions are not granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submission policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: To comply with ICML Dual Submission Policy, ensure a paper accepted or under review at another conference is not under submission to ICML 2026 by the full paper submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full paper deadline is after AISTATS 2026 and ICLR 2026 notifications, enabling removal of potential dual submissions in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed submission formats
rubrics_metrics.description: ICML 2026 accepts full (research) papers and position papers only; it is not possible to submit only an abstract or only a poster without a full paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An abstract must first be submitted by the abstract deadline; only after submitting the abstract can you upload the full paper PDF by the full paper deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation mode and attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference is planned as an in-person event with no support for virtual or hybrid presentation, though accepted authors are not required to attend and papers will still appear in proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proceedings-only papers, at least one author must obtain virtual registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: License selection and arXiv policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose an appropriate license per OpenReview legal terms; authors are allowed to post versions on preprint servers such as arXiv either before or while under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See OpenReview legal terms and arXiv license information page for related advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: No LaTeX template modification for space advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifying the ICML LaTeX template to gain an unfair 'space' advantage (e.g., by commenting-out \\printAffiliationsAndNotice) is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided template without manipulations intended to increase available space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest (COI) profile update procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Update COI information by signing into OpenReview, editing your profile (Emails, History, Relations sections). See ICML COI definitions for what constitutes a COI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure institutional email addresses are listed in the 'Emails' section; co-authors in publications imported from DBLP do not need to be manually added as relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind policy for links to code/data
rubrics_metrics.description: Including a link to code/data in a submission that contains identifying information (e.g., a GitHub username) violates double-blind policy and may lead to desk rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymize any code/data/links included in your submission to avoid de-anonymization risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer behavior regarding external searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should NOT search the internet (or elsewhere) for submissions they are assigned to review, as this could violate double-blind review; if reviewers have legitimately already seen de-anonymized versions (e.g., arXiv) this is acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a best practice, wait until you have read the paper at least once before doing a literature search on its topic.
